purpose: Structured seed catalog for future InkDrop provider registry and source-policy work.

mode_definitions.auto: Eligible for automatic search, candidate scoring, download, import, and verification when all provider gates pass.
mode_definitions.assist: Can produce candidates or metadata, but download/import needs explicit provider-specific approval or a later hardening gate.
mode_definitions.manual_review: Can show candidates or links to an operator, but InkDrop must not download automatically.
mode_definitions.metadata_only: Can enrich matching, aliases, identifiers, issue counts, release dates, or availability only.
mode_definitions.disabled: Known source or source family that must not be used by automation.

global_invariants: auto_download_allowed may only be true for sources with explicit rights, ownership, license, or public-domain gates.
shadow-library, paywall-bypass, adult, generic/unconfigured private-tracker, account-scrape, and CAPTCHA-gated sources must not be catalog-default auto providers.
download-capable providers must stage files, reject HTML/error pages, record source metadata, import normally, and verify in Kavita before resolving wanted rows.
Prowlarr-backed providers must store the real indexer name/id, category, seeders, info hash or download URL hash, and rejection reason.

Search-engine and reader-site providers may cache candidates for review by default; automatic retrieval requires a dedicated direct-file, header-probe, reader-pack, or indexer source primitive plus explicit user policy.

provider_candidates.first_ticket: Parse OPDS feeds, score title/author/language, and download EPUB through the shared direct downloader.
Use /books search with language and MIME filters, prefer EPUB, and persist Project Gutenberg id plus selected format URL.
Let users add OPDS/OPDS2 acquisition catalog URLs; parse acquisition links into direct candidates and route them through shared direct artifact and staging gates.
Search item metadata, fetch /metadata/{identifier}, choose one safe public file, and reject borrow-only/restricted/ocr-only comic candidates.

Use MangaDex API search and manga feed endpoints as settings-backed chapter evidence; when a user explicitly enables At-Home page fetching and auto policy gates, resolve matching chapter page URLs into the shared page-pack CBZ staging path.
Use a user-configured local Suwayomi server to search installed manga sources, fetch exact title/chapter matches, and package resolved page endpoints through InkDrop page-pack staging.

Treat a user-configured Suwayomi download folder as a watched source adapter: report/dry-run first, copy matching files into InkDrop staging, promote only strict wanted matches to import-ready, and verify through folder truth.
Use as metadata enrichment only until a WS export/download story is explicitly implemented.
Use identifiers, authors, editions, cover ids, and availability hints for matching; do not automate lending/download flows.
Keep as metadata and issue identity enrichment; never treat metadata presence as acquisition proof.
Use titles, synonyms, native title, dates, and format to improve MangaDex/manual matching.

provider_candidates.help_text: Optional open-license Internet Archive lane. Add it only when Prowlarr has a matching indexer and keep assisted review enabled for license validation.
provider_candidates.first_ticket: Add per-indexer policy and route promising results through Internet Archive metadata/file validation before download.

provider_candidates.help_text: Recommended manga preset for a configured Nyaa indexer in Prowlarr. Starts disabled; strict title, language, category, ownership, and seed gates apply when enabled.
provider_candidates.first_ticket: Target Nyaa manga indexers through editable indexer IDs, category gates, a categoryless Literature-indexer fallback for Prowlarr category-map misses, language gates, seed gates, manga scope checks, and normal download-client handoff policy.

provider_candidates.help_text: Recommended manga preset for a configured Tokyo Toshokan indexer in Prowlarr. Starts disabled and uses strict manga scope and seed gates.
provider_candidates.first_ticket: Target the local Prowlarr Tokyo Toshokan manga indexer through editable indexer IDs, category gates, language gates, seed gates, manga scope checks, and normal download-client handoff policy.

provider_candidates.help_text: Recommended comics preset for a configured TorrentLeech indexer in Prowlarr. Starts disabled and supports bounded issue and weekly-pack matching.
provider_candidates.first_ticket: Represent the local non-freeleech InkDrop comics clone as a settings-backed Prowlarr source so weekly-pack and issue searches can target it directly.

provider_candidates.help_text: Legacy compatibility preset for existing KAT-backed configurations. New setups should use Prowlarr discovery or a configured Torznab endpoint instead.
provider_candidates.first_ticket: Expose the configured-but-disabled KAT comics/manga Prowlarr indexer as an explicit user-enableable source lane; keep strict metadata, category, and seed gates before qBittorrent handoff.

provider_candidates.help_text: Legacy compatibility preset for existing Pirate Bay configurations. It is hidden from new-source defaults because public indexer identity and availability are unstable.
provider_candidates.first_ticket: Expose the configured-but-disabled Pirate Bay comics/ebook Prowlarr indexer as an explicit user-enableable source lane; keep strict ownership, category, and seed gates before qBittorrent handoff.

provider_candidates.help_text: Legacy compatibility preset for existing TorrentDownload configurations. New setups should use Prowlarr discovery or a configured Torznab endpoint instead.
provider_candidates.first_ticket: Expose the configured-but-disabled TorrentDownload comics/ebook Prowlarr indexer as an explicit user-enableable source lane; keep strict ownership, category, and seed gates before qBittorrent handoff.

provider_candidates.help_text: Recommended comics and magazine preset for a configured DOGnzb indexer in Prowlarr. Starts disabled and hands verified NZBs to SABnzbd.
provider_candidates.first_ticket: Represent the local DOGnzb comics Newznab indexer as a settings-backed Prowlarr source so weekly-pack and issue searches can prefer SAB/NZB handoff when strict manifest evidence is present.

provider_candidates.help_text: Legacy compatibility preset retained for persisted EBookBay configurations; it is not offered as a new default source.
provider_candidates.first_ticket: Represent as a named indexer with category and rejection diagnostics; do not auto-download.

provider_candidates.help_text: Compatibility definition for open datasets and educational material, which are outside InkDrop's supported comic, manga, and book import targets.
provider_candidates.first_ticket: Add settings-backed Prowlarr discovery for open educational results; keep download handoff disabled until InkDrop supports dataset/open-education import targets.

provider_candidates.help_text: Discovery-only compatibility definition. It cannot hand a verified acquisition to InkDrop and is hidden from new-source defaults.
provider_candidates.first_ticket: Treat as discovery only and require a real provider/indexer provenance before any download handoff.

provider_candidates.help_text: Add a Torznab-compatible endpoint you control. Requires a base URL and usually an API key; starts disabled and assisted until you review its categories and source policy.
provider_candidates.first_ticket: Let users add any Torznab/Jackett-compatible indexer endpoint with base URL, API secret, categories, and seed gates; parse RSS/XML results into indexer candidates and route them through normal download-client handoff policy.

provider_candidates.help_text: Add a Newznab-compatible endpoint you control. Requires a base URL and API key; starts disabled and assisted until you review its categories and SABnzbd handoff policy.
provider_candidates.first_ticket: Let users add any Newznab-compatible NZB indexer endpoint with base URL, API secret, and categories; parse RSS/XML NZB results into Usenet indexer candidates and route policy-safe auto sources through the SABnzbd handoff path.

provider_candidates.help_text: Add a trusted RSS or Atom feed that publishes magnets, torrent links, or labeled info hashes. Starts disabled and requires explicit source policy review.
provider_candidates.first_ticket: Let users add RSS/Atom feeds that publish magnet, torrent, or item-body labeled info-hash locators; parse release rows into indexer candidates and route them through normal seed, extension, pack, and download-client handoff policy.

provider_candidates.help_text: Add a trusted RSS or Atom feed whose items link to bounded torrent detail pages. Starts disabled and requires explicit source policy review.
provider_candidates.first_ticket: Let users add RSS/Atom feeds where matching feed items link to torrent detail pages before magnet, .torrent, or labeled info-hash locators appear; fetch a bounded number of detail pages and route policy-safe auto sources through the qBittorrent handoff path.

provider_candidates.help_text: Legacy compatibility template for persisted HTML scraper configurations. New sources should use Prowlarr, Torznab, Newznab, or RSS because arbitrary HTML selectors are brittle and noisy.
provider_candidates.first_ticket: Let users add torrent search result page URL templates and optional bounded pagination URL templates; parse only magnet anchors, direct .torrent anchors, or result-like blocks with a matching title and visible labeled info-hash locator into indexer candidates, then route policy-safe auto sources through the qBittorrent handoff path.

provider_candidates.help_text: Legacy compatibility template for persisted detail-page scraper configurations. New sources should use Prowlarr, Torznab, Newznab, or RSS because arbitrary page traversal is brittle and noisy.
provider_candidates.first_ticket: Let users add torrent HTML/JSON search URL templates, optional bounded pagination URL templates, or opt a base URL into the WordPress REST search flavor, for sources that require opening result/detail pages before magnet, .torrent, or labeled info-hash locators appear; fetch a bounded number of matching detail pages, parse only torrent locators, and route policy-safe auto sources through the qBittorrent handoff path.

Move feed attempts through provider registry, fetch a bounded number of matching post/detail pages from the feed, parse only explicit archive links from those pages, persist GUID/link/rejection reason, and suppress repeated bad packs.

Let users add RSS/Atom feeds that publish direct file enclosures or explicit archive/ebook links inside item description/content HTML; parse only those direct artifact URLs, size, and content type into direct candidates and route them through the shared direct artifact and staging gates.

Let users add explicit HTTP/HTTPS direct file URL sources only when InkDrop can prove the target is a bounded archive/ebook artifact through headers or bounded GET, then stage via the shared direct downloader with sidecar evidence.
Keep local/manual intake as a concrete inbox source: scan bounded local folders, validate archive-like files and safe paths, stage/copy into InkDrop import-ready flow, and preserve history/evidence.

Let users add RSS/Atom feeds where feed items link to post/detail pages before archive or ebook links appear; match wanted titles in feed items, fetch a bounded number of post pages, parse only explicit file links, and route policy-safe auto sources through the shared direct artifact and staging gates.

Let users add RSS/Atom feeds whose matching items link to DDL post/detail pages that expose extensionless download links or supported shared-file-host links; fetch bounded detail pages, rewrite supported shared hosts, prove final filename/content type/size with HEAD or bounded GET, and route only header-verified artifacts through shared direct staging gates.

provider_candidates.display_name: Generic RSS/Atom Reader Page Pack Feed
provider_candidates.first_ticket: Let users add RSS/Atom feeds whose matching items link to series, chapter, or reader pages; fetch a bounded number of feed-linked pages and chapter pages, extract ordered page image URLs, and route policy-safe sequences through the shared page-pack CBZ staging path.

Let users add search/list page URL templates and optional bounded pagination URL templates for sources that expose direct file links in href, button/input data URL attributes, form actions, simple click-navigation attributes, meta refresh targets, strict link rel download/enclosure/attachment metadata, JSON-LD/schema.org file URL fields, or explicit redirect query parameters whose decoded target is an allowed archive/ebook URL; parse only explicit archive/ebook links into direct candidates and route them through the shared direct artifact and staging gates.

Let users add HTML/JSON search page URL templates, optional bounded pagination URL templates, or opt a base URL into the WordPress REST search flavor, for sources that require opening result/detail pages before direct archive or ebook links appear; fetch a bounded number of detail pages from matching search-result links, parse only explicit file link/metadata elements, JSON-LD/schema.org file URL fields, or explicit redirect query parameters whose decoded target is an allowed archive/ebook URL, and route candidates through the shared direct artifact and staging gates.

Let users add HTML/JSON search page URL templates, optional bounded pagination URL templates, or opt a base URL into the WordPress REST search flavor, for DDL/blog sources whose detail pages expose extensionless download links or supported shared file-host links; fetch bounded detail pages from matching search-result links, rewrite Pixeldrain share URLs to the documented file endpoint when enabled, HEAD-probe or policy-opt-in bounded-GET probe download-looking links, derive filename/content type/size from headers or final URL/Location hints, and route only header-verified artifacts through the shared direct artifact and staging gates.

Let users add browser-reader or manga-reader search/list URL templates and optional bounded pagination URL templates; fetch a bounded number of series/detail pages and reader/chapter pages, extract ordered page image URLs, and route policy-safe sequences through a page-pack downloader that builds CBZ files for normal import.

Let users add JSON search/catalog endpoints, optional bounded pagination URL templates, or opt a base URL into the WordPress posts REST flavor, that expose explicit file/download URL fields or rendered HTML content containing allowed archive/ebook links; parse only explicit artifact URLs into direct candidates and route them through the shared direct artifact and staging gates.
Poll ComicsCodes feed/list pages as source evidence, record URL/title/backoff outcomes, and keep resolver/download handoff behind a later hardened provider gate.

Add dry-run/search adapter by default, capture version/stdout/stderr, expose structured command_executable/command_args settings for injected runner execution, and allow import-ready handoff only when an explicit user policy supplies a sandboxed staged-output root.

Expose as a settings-backed external-tool bridge; capture search/dry-run output as review evidence by default, expose structured command_executable/command_args settings for injected runner execution, and allow import-ready handoff only when an explicit user policy supplies a sandboxed staged-output root.

Expose as a settings-backed external-tool bridge; require connector-specific dry-run evidence by default, expose structured command_executable/command_args settings for injected runner execution, and allow import-ready handoff only when an explicit user policy supplies a sandboxed staged-output root.

Define bridge contract after Comic-DL proof; keep per-connector enablement, no credential/CAPTCHA bypass, expose structured command_executable/command_args settings for injected runner execution, and allow import-ready handoff only when an explicit user policy supplies a sandboxed staged-output root.

Use user-configured search URL templates and optional bounded pagination URL templates to fetch reader-site search/list pages automatically; cache result metadata only and require provider-specific validation for any page/download resolver.

Use user-configured search URL templates and optional bounded pagination URL templates to fetch DDL/blog result pages automatically; cache result metadata only and require provider-specific validation for anything beyond review evidence.

Use user-configured search URL templates and optional bounded pagination URL templates to fetch book-search result pages automatically; cache result metadata only and require provider-specific validation for anything beyond review evidence.

Use user-configured search URL templates and optional bounded pagination URL templates to fetch public/free catalog pages automatically; split into individual API/direct providers only when rights and direct-file behavior are clear.
No implementation ticket; explicitly excluded from comics/manga/ebook automation.

Use user-configured search URL templates and optional bounded pagination URL templates to fetch shadow-library/search-portal result pages automatically; record review evidence only and require a provider-specific resolver before any download handoff.
No implementation ticket for current InkDrop automation.
No implementation until an explicit account-compliant and lawful integration policy exists.
Defer until InkDrop explicitly supports audiobook media and rights/provider policy.
